title: Constrained Engineering Optimization System
objective: Find useful design parameters for a simulated engineering-style objective under explicit constraints.

milestones.title: Define objective functions, bounds, and linear/nonlinear constraints.
acceptance_criteria: Demonstrate: Define objective functions, bounds, and linear/nonlinear constraints.
Include a reproducible test or verification step.

acceptance_criteria: Demonstrate: Compare local and global optimization methods where appropriate.

starter_files.purpose: Setup, run instructions, scope, assumptions, and expected deliverables.
Small runnable starting point for the analysis pipeline.
Tests for known results, boundaries, invalid values, and tolerance-based numeric checks.

required_features: Define objective functions, bounds, and linear/nonlinear constraints.
Compare local and global optimization methods where appropriate.
Inspect convergence diagnostics and constraint satisfaction.
Perform sensitivity analysis and document model limitations.
stretch_features: Add an independent method and explain when the two methods disagree.
Add a synthetic edge-case dataset and automated regression tests.
Provide an optional labeled visualization while keeping calculations separate from presentation.

tests.name: Numerical correctness
steps: Compare at least one result with a known synthetic answer or independent method.
Use scale-aware tolerances where floating-point approximation is expected.

tests.name: Boundaries and failure modes
steps: Test empty, non-finite, malformed, or boundary inputs where relevant.
Do not report success when a solver or input validation step fails.

tests.name: Reproducibility
steps: Run with documented dependencies and a fixed random seed if randomness is involved.
Record the SciPy version, units, assumptions, and method settings.

rubric.criterion: Mathematical/scientific correctness and appropriate method selection
Numerical validation, error checks, and boundary handling
Input validation and treatment of assumptions/uncertainty

review_method: Automated local tests plus human rubric review. The production API is not an arbitrary Python execution environment; submissions require an isolated runner or human review.
status_note: Draft project brief derived from Section D of the supplied SciPy PDF; full implementation, tests, data assumptions, and rubric require human review before publication.
